theory: Qualify the definite-integral statement with existence, consistent with the booklet's continuity and discontinuity discussion at lines 1176–1192. Clarify that one arbitrary constant is sufficient, while several additive arbitrary constants are equivalent and merely redundant; they must not be taught as mathematically wrong.

summary: Removed unsupported recognition, error-explanation and comparison tasks, replaced quotient and initial-condition tasks with supported general-primitive questions, and confined the paired integration item to indefinite integration. Qualified the theory's definite-integral statement with existence, clarified that additive arbitrary constants are equivalent but redundant, and repaired quiz q3's duplicate correct option while preserving unaffected content.
reviewSummary: All 20 final items have correct answers, use supported booklet question types and remain within the target scope; every quiz has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations.
